method: Individual review against PDF pages 27–33; neutral teaching examples replace mismatched or unnecessarily graphic source-derived examples while source excerpts remain intact. Allegations and narrator inferences remain distinguished.
words: to help an activity or process happen more easily
Connect facilitate with facility as something that makes an activity easier. A facilitator helps a group work, rather than doing every task personally.
The coordinator helped facilitate the discussion.
协调员协助推动了讨论。
One of the staff member's organizational tasks; source leaves the object unstated, so none is inserted into the quote.
a trained or experienced person paid to do a job
与受雇的专业人员合作
Hire means employ for payment; professional identifies a paid specialist. Distinguish this role from a student volunteer.
The repairs were handled by a hired professional.
维修由受雇的专业人员负责。
Source contrasts employee role with student peer; paid professional does not itself guarantee competence or conduct.
a person responsible for managing a residential house or facility
Director directs operations; house tells you the workplace. Picture someone managing residential facilities rather than directing a film.
The house director arranged the repairs.
The narrator's explanation of house mom; not necessarily a university employee.
the minimum age at which a person is legally permitted to drink alcohol in the relevant setting
Legal modifies the permitted age, not the type of drink. Learn of legal drinking age as a fixed description of eligibility.
The staff checked whether guests were of legal drinking age.
工作人员检查了来宾是否达到法定饮酒年龄。
Language gloss for the narrated setting; no jurisdiction-wide statement of current age exceptions or legal advice.
relating to the practical running of an organization or activity
运营方面的；日常运作的
operation + -al gives operational. Here it concerns day-to-day running; an operational machine has a different sense, functioning and ready to use.
Modifies manager in source; not a statement about equipment being functional.
a manager responsible for an organization's everyday activities
运营经理；日常事务主管
Manage names the action, manager the person, and operational the area of responsibility. Operations manager is another common job-title form.
The operational manager coordinated the daily schedule.
运营经理协调了日常安排。
Preserves source's operational manager rather than silently changing it to the more common operations manager.
to supervise and take responsibility for an activity
over + see suggests watching over an activity. Distinguish oversee, supervise, from overlook, fail to notice.
她负责监管这栋楼的维护工作。
Supervisory role, not simply seeing the building from above.
paid a regular salary for work
salary changes y to -ied in salaried. Attach the word to regular pay, not a guarantee of a particular salary amount.
The organization hired a salaried administrator.
该组织聘请了一名领取固定薪水的行政人员。
Paid employee contrasted with undergraduate peer; no actual employment contract verified.
small servings of strong alcoholic drink
Shot has several meanings; shots of vodka anchors the small-drink sense, not gunfire or photographs. The plural ends /ts/.
The menu listed shots of several spirits.
菜单列出了几种按小杯供应的烈酒。
Reported drinking quantity; does not define a universal serving volume or encourage consumption.
a university student studying toward a first degree
Undergraduate is before completing a first degree; graduate can describe someone who has completed one. Here -ate has a reduced ending, not the verb sound /eɪt/.
The program is open to undergraduate students.
这个项目面向本科生开放。
Peer-student role contrasted with house director, not a description of the staff member.
work or expense needed to keep something in good condition
Keep up something's condition becomes the noun upkeep. Picture recurring cleaning and repairs, not a one-time construction project.
The fees help pay for the building's upkeep.
这些费用用于分担建筑维护开支。
a strong, usually clear distilled alcoholic drink
Remember VOD-ka in two syllables with stress first. Keep the /dk/ consonants together and use vodka as a drink name, not a countable glass.
The report mentioned a bottle of vodka.
报告提到了一瓶伏特加。
Specific spirit named in allegations; later beer comparison is narrator speculation, not equivalent drink quantities.
a person employed to control entry and keep order at a bar or club
酒吧或夜店门口的保安
bounce + -er names a person in this informal job title. Picture the entry-control role rather than a person physically bouncing.
The bouncer checked the guests' IDs.
门口保安检查了来宾的证件。
The speaker assumes an ID check; that assumption is not converted into a verified original quote.
a person responsible for looking after people, a building, or property
care + taker is someone who takes care of something. Here the role includes a residence and its occupants, not necessarily medical care.
The resident caretaker reported the broken door.
驻楼管理员报告了损坏的门。
Role description in narration, not proof of a legally defined duty in this case.
a person who prepares and serves drinks at a bar
酒吧调酒师；吧台服务员
bar + tender: tend means look after or serve. A bartender tends the bar, not the door like a bouncer.
The bartender offered the guest a soft drink.
吧台服务员给这位客人提供了一杯软饮料。
Drink-service staff are the intended readers of the hand marks in the account.
a business or public place such as a bar, restaurant, or hotel
establish + -ment can mean the act of founding or the place founded. Here at this establishment points to the bar, not the political establishment.
这家营业场所午夜关门。
Place/business sense; allegations about service remain attributed to the lawsuit.
a fellow member of a college fraternity
Brother is organizational kinship here, not a biological sibling. Combine it with fraternity to specify shared membership.
He met a fraternity brother at the reunion.
他在聚会上见到了一位同会成员。
Shared organization, not family relationship or proof of involvement in an allegation.
different or not joined to something else
The adjective separate ends /rət/; the verb separate ends /reɪt/. Remember the middle spelling -para-, not -pera-.
The meeting will be held in a separate room.
会议将在另一间房间举行。
Adjective in a separate bar; distinguish venues instead of merging allegations about them.
未满二十一岁标识腕带
Under before a number means below that limit. Under 21 excludes exactly 21; use a hyphen when it modifies wristband.
Guests under 21 received a different wristband.
未满二十一岁的宾客领到了不同的腕带。
Age label in the account, not a statement about all legal rules in every jurisdiction.
a band worn around the wrist, often for identification or entry
wrist + band names where the band goes. The w in wrist is silent; contrast wristband with waistband at the waist.
Each visitor received an identification wristband.
每位访客都领到了一条身份识别腕带。
Age/status marker, not by itself evidence that drinks were served.
in an uncomfortable or socially uneasy way
awkward + -ly describes how an action feels or happens. Pair awkwardly sitting with an uncomfortable silence, not necessarily physical clumsiness.
They smiled awkwardly after the misunderstanding.
误会发生后，他们尴尬地笑了笑。
Narrator's impression of the seating interaction, introduced by I guess.
a long upholstered seat for more than one person
Couch rhymes with ouch, not coach. Picture several people sitting on one long seat.
We sat on the couch and talked.
Furniture noun; not the verb couch a statement in particular terms.
moving the body rhythmically, usually to music
dance drops final e before -ing: dancing. Keep the /s/ sound from dance; it does not become /k/.
They started dancing when the music began.
音乐响起时，他们开始跳舞。
Reported activity; dancing does not imply consent to later sexual acts.
made a proposal to someone, especially a sexual invitation
Proposition is a proposal; proposition someone is often a sexual proposition, unlike propose a work plan. Add -ed without another syllable after /n/.
She reported that a stranger had propositioned her.
她报告称，一个陌生人向她提出了性邀约。
The source attributes the proposition to her lawsuit; the verb itself does not establish consent or coercion.
not known, certain, or easy to understand
un- negates clear. Separate unclear evidence from something disproved: unclear means not established either way.
It remains unclear how long the delay will last.
延误会持续多久仍不清楚。
Actual dancing duration is expressly uncertain despite one person's estimate.
a room named for former students or members; here, the fraternity's own room label
校友室（此处为兄弟会房间名称）
Alumni are former students; alumni room is a room label, not proof that only alumni use it. Remember label and actual use can differ.
The tour included a room called the alumni room.
参观行程包括了一间名为校友室的房间。
Source describes mixed bedroom/social use; not a standardized room type with guaranteed access rules.
to gather together in a group
Connect congregate with congregation, a gathered group. The verb ends /ɡeɪt/ and pictures many people coming together.
Students often congregate in the courtyard.
学生们经常聚集在庭院里。
Gathering place, not a claim that every member was present.
Proof here measures alcoholic strength, not evidence. Hyphenate high-proof when it comes before the drink name.
The article referred to high-proof spirits.
Believed to be qualifies identification; no exact concentration inferred.
Remember marijuana with the /wɑ/ sound in the stressed syllable; the written j does not sound like the j in job.
The report mentioned alleged marijuana use.
报告提到了据称存在的大麻使用。
Substance name in a pleading; no use guidance or diagnosis.
the person or organization bringing a civil lawsuit
Connect plaintiff with complaint and contrast it with defendant. Keep double f and remember that a legal role is not a finding of truth.
The plaintiff submitted a written statement.
原告提交了一份书面陈述。
Role of the complainant in quoted legal wording, not interchangeable with prosecutor.
like powder or consisting of fine dry particles
powder + -y gives powdery. The adjective describes appearance or texture and does not identify the chemical substance.
A powdery layer covered the shelf.
架子上覆着一层粉末状的东西。
White powder appearance is separate from the attributed claim that it was ketamine.
trying to make someone do something through persistent influence or demands
pressure drops final e before -ing. Learn pressure someone into + -ing, with the person between verb and into.
They were accused of pressuring staff into working late.
他们被指责向员工施压，要求员工加班。
Pressure allegation remains attributed; teaching example transfers structure to a work setting.
drawing a powdered substance into the nose; also making a sharp nasal sound in other contexts
有关经鼻吸入毒品的指称
Snort can be a sharp nose sound; in this context it describes intake through the nose. Keep -ing attached to snort without changing the base.
The report included allegations of snorting a substance.
报告包含有关经鼻吸入某种物质的指称。
Receptive vocabulary only; no technique or dosage is supplied.
Substance can mean material or meaningful content. A bag containing a substance anchors the material sense, without guessing its identity.
The container held an unknown substance.
容器里装着一种不明物质。
Identification is nested attribution: Jane says they said it was ketamine, not a confirmed laboratory finding.
让房间保持未上锁状态
un- reverses locked. Locked and unlocked both end /kt/; add no extra vowel after k.
The side door was left unlocked.
Physical access state, not proof that the room was open to everyone with permission.
the state of the penis becoming firm and enlarged
Erect can mean upright; erection names a resulting state. Context determines the anatomical sense rather than construction of a building.
The clinical report mentioned difficulty maintaining an erection.
临床报告提到了难以维持勃起的情况。
Anatomical term in an attributed assault account; teaching example is clinical, not erotic or diagnostic.
during the same period of time
meanwhile links simultaneous timelines. While already signals time; meanwhile introduces what another person is doing during that period.
I prepared the slides. Meanwhile, my colleague checked the figures.
我准备幻灯片。与此同时，同事核对了数据。
Signals concurrent actions, not permission or causal connection.
a message sent to several people in a shared conversation
Group identifies the audience; message is the communication. A group message can reach many recipients without proving each read it.
She sent a group message about the meeting.
她发送了一条有关会议的群消息。
Source alleges a message to a chapter chat; recipients are not automatically participants in the events.
the name of a social messaging application
The brand combines snap, a quick picture, and chat, conversation. Preserve its capital S as a proper name.
The report referred to a Snapchat group.
报告提到了一个 Snapchat 群组。
Brand/platform identification only; no assumptions about current features or message persistence.
located or working at the place where an activity takes place
on + site means at the actual location. On-site is an alternative spelling; distinguish site, a place, from sight, seeing.
An onsite manager handled the issue.
一位驻场经理处理了这个问题。
Manager lives/works at the house in the narration; not an online role.
a person responsible for directing work or running an organization or facility
manage drops final e before -er: manager. The suffix names the person who manages, not the task itself.
The manager arranged a meeting with the staff.
经理安排了与员工的会议。
Paid management role, contrasted with elected student president.
people paid to work for an employer
Employer hires; employee is hired. The -ee ending often identifies the receiver of an action; plural employees ends /iz/.
The organization has several full-time employees.
该组织有几名全职员工。
Source asks whether they are school employees and answers no; retain that distinction.
employed or engaged to do paid work
hire already ends in e, so add d: hired. Connect hired with paid employment rather than biological/family ties.
She was hired to manage the residence.
Employment relationship as described, not proof of a specific employment contract.
regards or thinks of something in a particular way
consider + -s is third-person singular. Learn consider something + noun/adjective; no as is required in considers it a room.
The team considers it a useful starting point.
团队认为这是一个有用的起点。
Regard-as sense, not the separate sense of weighing an option before deciding.
a person or organization against whom a legal case is brought
Connect defendant with defend: the party answers or defends against a claim. Being named a defendant is not being found liable.
The company was named as a defendant in the lawsuit.
该公司被列为这起诉讼的被告。
The narration explicitly distinguishes named defendants from people/venues not named.
asked someone to come to a place or event
invite ends in /t/, so invited adds /ɪd/. Invite somebody to a place/event differs from invite somebody to do something.
She invited her friends over for dinner.
她邀请朋友们来吃晚饭。
Identifies the person who invited her; accepting an invitation does not imply consent to later acts.
thought to be true or to have a particular identity, without certainty
believe adds d to become believed. In believed to be, the passive wording reports a belief rather than proving the claim.
The object was believed to be an old tool.
这件物品被认为是一件旧工具。
Qualifies high-proof rum identification; does not establish actual substance or strength.
